name: Oberhofen im Inntal
kurzbeschreibung: Warm and welcoming community in the Inntal valley, featuring the stunning blue Oberhofen lake and natural living between the Inn river and the highway.
beschreibung:
Overview

Oberhofen im Inntal is situated in the upper Inn Valley within the Innsbruck-Land district, approximately 25 kilometers west of Innsbruck and only five kilometers southeast of the market town of Telfs at an altitude of 622 meters. Home to roughly 1,920 residents, this peaceful residential community extends across a gently raised, sun-kissed alluvial terrace on the southern bank of the Inn River, nestling at the foot of the northern Stubai Alps beneath the Rietzer Grießkogel and Flaurlinger Joch. Looking across the river, visitors are treated to an awe-inspiring panorama of the sheer 1,500-meter south face of the Hohe Munde (2,662 m) and the jagged crests of the Mieming Range. Oberhofen preserves an authentic pastoral charm, serving as an idyllic base for river cyclists, alpine pasture hikers, and nature lovers seeking calm away from busy traffic.

History

Human habitation in Oberhofen has ancient roots, corroborated by Iron Age artifacts and exceptional bronze statuettes of a warrior discovered in the Pircherwald forest. The earliest official documentation dates back to October 28, 799, under the name 'Oparinhofe', when nobleman Gaio bequeathed his valley lands to the Bavarian monastery of Schlehdorf, making Oberhofen one of the oldest documented settlements in the Inn Valley. The town crest still bears two crossed water lily leaves in tribute to Schlehdorf Abbey. A chapel dedicated to St. Nicholas was confirmed by Pope Alexander III in 1177. Between 1740 and 1742, master builder Gallus Gratl constructed the present Baroque parish church of St. Nicholas in the village center, adorned with ceiling frescoes by Anton Zoller. Inside the historic town house, a charming local history museum preserves rural crafts and village heritage.

Getting There

Oberhofen enjoys first-class transport links within the central Tyrolean transit network. By car, drivers take the A12 Inntal Autobahn to exit Telfs Ost or Zirl West, following the B171 or the L11 provincial road south of the river, arriving in about 25 minutes from Innsbruck. Rail travelers benefit from the dedicated Oberhofen im Inntal station on the Arlberg Railway: Tyrolean S-Bahn lines S4 and S5 run every 30 minutes directly to Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof (a quick 22-minute ride) as well as westward to Telfs-Pfaffenhofen and Landeck. Regional VVT buses complement the train service, while touring cyclists enjoy direct access along the paved Inn River Cycle Path (R3).

Tips

A prime hiking destination high above the valley is the Oberhofer Melkalm at 1,668 meters, commanding panoramic vistas across the Inn Valley and linking into the scenic Peter Anich High Trail. In the adjacent Flaurling valley, the traditional Oberhofer Galtalm serves alpine cheese made on-site. Mountaineers can tackle the summit of the 2,884-meter Rietzer Grießkogel or cross the Flaurlinger Joch. Nature enthusiasts cycling the Inn River Cycle Path should visit the nearby Inzinger Gaisau nature reserve, one of Tyrol's premier protected wetland sanctuaries providing refuge to kingfishers and rare Siberian irises. Walking along the Tyrolean Way of St. James through the village meadows affords breathtaking photographic views of the Hohe Munde.
